items.body:
`build/compile_commands.json` gets generated currently through CMake.
But there are usually three compile commands per file, due to the different targets we have (nvim, libnvim, nvim-test).

This causes `clang-check` to run 3 commands (basically the same, but different in terms of defines etc).

Usually you would symlink `build/compile_commands.json` into the project root (to not have to use `-p` with `clang-check`, `clang-tidy` etc, and therefore we could provide a Makefile target to create a cleaned up version:

```make
# Massage compile_commands.json: keep first entry only (from the main nvim target).
# Using `unique_by(.file)` would not keep the order.
# jq 'unique_by(.file)' < $< > $<.tmp
compile_commands.json: build/compile_commands.json Makefile
       jq '[reduce .[] as $$x ({}; $$x.file as $$key | if .[$$key] then . else .[$$key] = $$x end) | .[]]' < $< > $<.tmp
       mv $<.tmp $@
```

Arguably it is more an issue with CMake, which could allow to configure what commands should be generated (e.g. for certain targets only, https://gitlab.kitware.com/cmake/cmake/issues/19462), or clang's tooling, which could have an option to only run the first found command.
However, Neovim could help its developers in this regard, given the current limitations.

E.g. these are the commands for `edit.c`:
```
  "command": "/usr/local/bin/cc -DINCLUDE_GENERATED_DECLARATIONS -DNVIM_MSGPACK_HAS_FLOAT32 -DNVIM_UNIBI_HAS_VAR_FROM -D_GNU_SOURCE -Dnvim_test_EXPORTS -Iconfig -I../src -Isrc/nvim/auto -Iinclude -I/usr/include/luajit-2.0 -isystem ../.deps/usr/include   -Werror -g -fPIC    -DUNIT_TESTING  -Wall -Wextra -pedantic -Wno-unused-parameter -Wstrict-prototypes -std=gnu99 -Wshadow -Wconversion -Wmissing-prototypes -Wimplicit-fallthrough -Wvla -fstack-protector-strong -fdiagnostics-color=always  -Wno-conversion -o src/nvim/CMakeFiles/nvim-test.dir/edit.c.o   -c …/Vcs/neovim/src/nvim/edit.c",
  "command": "/usr/local/bin/cc -DINCLUDE_GENERATED_DECLARATIONS -DNVIM_MSGPACK_HAS_FLOAT32 -DNVIM_UNIBI_HAS_VAR_FROM -D_GNU_SOURCE -Iconfig -I../src -Isrc/nvim/auto -Iinclude -I/usr/include/luajit-2.0 -isystem ../.deps/usr/include   -Werror -g   -Wall -Wextra -pedantic -Wno-unused-parameter -Wstrict-prototypes -std=gnu99 -Wshadow -Wconversion -Wmissing-prototypes -Wimplicit-fallthrough -Wvla -fstack-protector-strong -fdiagnostics-color=always  -Wno-conversion -o src/nvim/CMakeFiles/nvim.dir/edit.c.o   -c …/Vcs/neovim/src/nvim/edit.c",
  "command": "/usr/local/bin/cc -DINCLUDE_GENERATED_DECLARATIONS -DNVIM_MSGPACK_HAS_FLOAT32 -DNVIM_UNIBI_HAS_VAR_FROM -D_GNU_SOURCE -Iconfig -I../src -Isrc/nvim/auto -Iinclude -I/usr/include/luajit-2.0 -isystem ../.deps/usr/include   -Werror -g -fPIC    -DMAKE_LIB  -Wall -Wextra -pedantic -Wno-unused-parameter -Wstrict-prototypes -std=gnu99 -Wshadow -Wconversion -Wmissing-prototypes -Wimplicit-fallthrough -Wvla -fstack-protector-strong -fdiagnostics-color=always  -Wno-conversion -o src/nvim/CMakeFiles/libnvim.dir/edit.c.o   -c …/Vcs/neovim/src/nvim/edit.c",
```

Another option would be to use options to only build/configure the main target (by having CMake options `BUILD_LIBNVIM` and `BUILD_NVIMTEST` to control/skip those), but with regard to the compilation DB this is more of a hack (although it could be useful in general?!).
```diff
 CMakeLists.txt          | 2 +-
 src/nvim/CMakeLists.txt | 6 ++++++
 2 files changed, 7 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git i/CMakeLists.txt w/CMakeLists.txt
index b20345570..fc10cc9c2 100644
--- i/CMakeLists.txt
+++ w/CMakeLists.txt
@@ -588,7 +588,7 @@ if(BUSTED_PRG)
     message(WARNING "disabling unit tests: no Luajit FFI in ${LUA_PRG}")
   endif()
 
-  if(LUA_HAS_FFI)
+  if(BUILD_NVIMTEST AND LUA_HAS_FFI)
     set(TEST_LIBNVIM_PATH $<TARGET_FILE:nvim-test>)
   else()
     set(TEST_LIBNVIM_PATH "")
diff --git i/src/nvim/CMakeLists.txt w/src/nvim/CMakeLists.txt
index 0fc7c780c..df2f2a7e4 100644
--- i/src/nvim/CMakeLists.txt
+++ w/src/nvim/CMakeLists.txt
@@ -1,4 +1,6 @@
 option(USE_GCOV "Enable gcov support" OFF)
+option(BUILD_NVIMTEST "Build nvim-test (unit tests) target" ON)
+option(BUILD_LIBNVIM "Build libnvim target" ON)
 
 if(NOT CLANG_TSAN)
 # GCOV and TSAN results in false data race reports
@@ -487,6 +489,7 @@ else()
 endif()
 set_target_properties(nvim_runtime_deps PROPERTIES FOLDER deps)
 
+if(BUILD_LIBNVIM)
 add_library(
   libnvim
   STATIC
@@ -507,7 +510,9 @@ set_property(
   TARGET libnvim
   APPEND_STRING PROPERTY COMPILE_FLAGS " -DMAKE_LIB "
 )
+endif()
 
+if(BUILD_NVIMTEST)
 if(NOT LUAJIT_FOUND)
   message(STATUS "luajit not found, skipping nvim-test (unit tests) target")
 else()
@@ -537,6 +542,7 @@ else()
     APPEND_STRING PROPERTY COMPILE_FLAGS " -DUNIT_TESTING "
   )
 endif()
+endif()
 
 if(CLANG_ASAN_UBSAN)
   message(STATUS "Enabling Clang address sanitizer and undefined behavior sanitizer for nvim.")
```

(As for Neomake, I plan to have a maker/linter based on looking up the compile command in this JSON file, and there it would just use the first entry.)
